prompts: The game went down in June and we owe the team an incident report. The logs and their notes are in {WS}/logs. When did it start and end, how long was it, did we keep our monthly availability target, and why did it happen? Record it in {WS}/result.json: start, end, minutes_down, availability_june_pct, slo_999_ok, root_cause.
answers:
[goal] June incident report: window, duration, SLO, root cause → `./result.json`.

[action] Read `logs/README.md` (defines: down = first save error → "server ready"; SLO 99.9%; one incident), grepped all 3 logs (5396 lines) for error/fatal/ready/disk lines, timed the window, computed availability over 30 days = 43200 min.

[result] `./result.json` (valid JSON, verified by re-parse):
- start `2026-06-02T03:17:42` (first `ERROR SaveGame failed: ... No space left on device`, line 251)
- end `2026-06-02T03:53:31` (`INFO server ready, accepting players`, line 294)
- minutes_down `35.82` (35 min 49 s = 2149 s)
- availability_june_pct `99.9171` → slo_999_ok `true` (budget at 99.9% is 43.2 min; we used 35.8)
- root cause: `/data` full. `WARN disk /data usage 97% (free 3.1 GB)` at 03:10:02 → autosave ENOSPC → unresponsive → `FATAL watchdog` → 41 restart attempts all `exited code 137` → recovered only after `backup rotation freed 38.2 GB` at 03:52:10.

Assumptions: timestamps are local/server-clock, single timezone; availability counts the whole June (43200 min) with this one outage as the only downtime; minutes_down rounded to 2 decimals.

Excluded as noise: `RCON auth failed from 203.0.113.12` on 06-01 (auth noise, no downtime); `mem_gb` 21.8–28.6 across the whole window, so exit 137 is the watchdog's SIGKILL, not OOM.

[nnext] Optional follow-ups: alert on `/data` > 90% and make backup rotation run before the save path, not after; add a disk-full-aware restart backoff so the watchdog stops burning 41 attempts.
